At the age of 25, the patient was diagnosed with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis with exocrine and endocrine insufficiency.

Treatment was initiated with calcium (1200 mg) and vitamin D (800 IU) supplementation, along with a short course of GC at a target dose of 0.6 mg/kg for 4 weeks. Due to concerns that GC therapy might worsen osteoporosis, the patient was transferred to the Endocrinology Department.
The patient was started on prednisolone (0.6 mg/kg) and azathioprine (50 mg/day) maintenance therapy; however, due to poor tolerance, it was replaced with mycophenolate mofetil (250 mg/day).
After the administration of prednisolone and mycophenolate mofetil, the patient’s condition improved significantly.
A review of previous laboratory findings indicated that elevated IgG4 levels (up to 2 g/L) had been present since 2018.
This was the case for our patient, as she had significantly elevated serum IgG4 levels (2 g/L), as well as clinical and radiological signs characteristic of IgG4-RD.

summary.text: A 41-year-old woman was hospitalized in the Gastroenterology Department with severe generalized pruritus, salivary gland hypertrophy and tenderness, pain under the left rib cage and white-colored diarrhea. She had been diagnosed at age 25 with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis with exocrine and endocrine insufficiency, and had marked weight loss, osteoporosis and recurrent sialadenitis.

Her BMI was 11.97 kg/m^(2). A psychiatric assessment did not confirm an eating disorder. Laboratory tests showed hypokalemia, elevated alpha-amylase, normal pancreatic amylase and increased bile acids; imaging showed pancreatic calcifications, a dilated pancreatic duct with an intraductal stone, and heterogeneous parotid glands.

IgG4-RD was diagnosed clinically with chronic autoimmune pancreatitis and autoimmune sialadenitis; early-stage IgG4-related cholangitis could not be excluded. Salivary gland biopsy yielded insufficient tissue for immunohistochemistry.

Treatment began with calcium, vitamin D and a short glucocorticoid course; she was transferred to Endocrinology because of osteoporosis concerns. She was then started on prednisolone and azathioprine, which was replaced by mycophenolate mofetil because of poor tolerance, with denosumab for osteoporosis and supportive care. Rituximab was not required.
Her condition improved: pruritus resolved, IgG4 fell to 0.7 g/L, bile acids reached 4 µmol/L, the salivary glands returned to normal size and weight increased by 4 kg.
